expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: export type Subscription = TrialingSub | ActiveSub | PastDueSub | CanceledSub; with each variant having status: "trialing" | "active" | "past_due" | "canceled"

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: TrialingSub has trialEndDate, CanceledSub has only cancelReason/wasVoluntary; "You can't accidentally access trialEndDate on a canceled sub"

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: No assertNever, no switch statement, no never arm anywhere; only the claim "Adding a new status causes compile errors everywhere it's unhandled"

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: id: string; customerId: string; planId: string; — bare strings, no branding

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: No transition function or state-change constraint; response covers only type shapes and a cancelReason question

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: "You can't accidentally access `trialEndDate` on a canceled sub" and "TypeScript enforces that you handle each case"

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: "Discriminated unions beat optional fields here"; primary recommendation is the union with no optional fields
